Today, Apple held an opening ceremony for its advanced manufacturing center in Houston, Texas. The following are the relevant details.

Apple will provide training for business leaders at the newly opened Houston Advanced Manufacturing Center

Apple today opened its brand-new Advanced Manufacturing Center (AMC) in Houston. The center offers free training and educational courses for small and medium-sized businesses, allowing them to get hands-on experience with the most advanced equipment, interactive labs, and various tools to accelerate innovation. The Advanced Manufacturing Center is located at the same site as the Houston facility that produces and ships Apple's advanced AI servers, and will begin producing Mac mini later this year⋯⋯ Apple CEO Tim Cook said: "In just nine months, we have invested hundreds of millions of dollars in this Houston facility. We have built the factory, commenced production, and shipped the first batch of advanced AI servers from this facility. Today we are thrilled to unveil this brand-new Advanced Manufacturing Center, which will serve as a place for business leaders, workers, and students to learn the same set of innovative processes we use to manufacture Apple's most groundbreaking products. We also look forward to commencing production of Mac mini later this year. We believe in the strength of American workers and the creativity of America, and we are moving forward at a remarkable pace, because what we want to create is not just exceptional products — what we want to build is the future of American manufacturing."

Tim Cook announced his Houston trip via social media and specifically traveled there in person to attend the opening ceremony. Guests attending the ceremony included U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, U.S. Senator Ted Cruz, Houston Mayor John Whitmire, U.S. Congressman Christian Menefee, and Harris County Precinct One Commissioner Rodney Ellis.

The Advanced Manufacturing Center covers an area of 20,000 square feet, and Apple's experts will "share knowledge directly with participating businesses and entrepreneurs within the center, helping to accelerate the development of intelligent manufacturing in America."

The first batch of business leaders arrived today to attend the unveiling training sessions. The topics of the day centered on intelligent manufacturing technologies, including "machine learning-driven quality control and advanced automation."
